skill.name: dfam-check
skill.description: Measure mesh files against Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM) rules and report printability findings per process (FDM, SLS, SLA/DLP, metal PBF, MJF). Use when the user asks whether a part is printable, wants overhang/wall-thickness/support analysis of an `.stl`, `.obj`, `.ply`, or `.3mf` mesh, wants a build-orientation recommendation, or wants DfAM redesign guidance before slicing with `$gcode` or regenerating geometry with `$cad`.
skill.summary: Measure mesh geometry and compare printability against process-specific DfAM limits.
skill.author: earthtojake

content.user_title: Check Mesh Printability Before You Print
content.value_statement: Mesh files often fail during slicing because walls, overhangs, units, or topology were not checked against the selected process. This skill measures those geometry facts locally and turns them into evidence-based DfAM guidance.
actual_capabilities: Measures mesh bounds, volume, surface area, triangle count, watertightness, Euler number, and body count.
Samples wall thickness per connected body and reports minimum, percentile, median, and maximum values.
Maps down-facing faces against a selected self-supporting angle.
Estimates support volume and compares six axis-aligned build orientations.
Compares measured facts with process limits for FDM, SLS, SLA/DLP, metal PBF, and MJF.
Provides redesign guidance and identifies measurements that require more information.
limitations: It does not slice meshes, create print jobs, upload files, or control printers.
Wall thickness uses sampling, so it is not an exhaustive inspection of every location.
Support volume is a coarse upper-bound estimate, not a slicer result.
Hole diameter, positive features, bridges, and trapped powder are not measured directly.

use_cases.title: Validate a prototype mesh
use_cases.description: Check walls, overhangs, scale, and watertightness before sending a prototype to a print service.

use_cases.title: Compare manufacturing processes
use_cases.description: Evaluate one mesh against candidate process limits and identify which measurements need process-specific data.

use_cases.title: Prepare a redesign review
use_cases.description: Use measured failures and orientation tradeoffs to create concrete geometry changes before CAD regeneration.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Printability Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the attached mesh for printability. Ask for the target process if it is missing, then report the measured geometry facts and the main risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single mesh

prompt_templates.title: Process Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this mesh for FDM, SLS, SLA/DLP, metal PBF, and MJF. Use the process limits reference, separate measured results from missing checks, and explain the strongest constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Orientation Recommendation
prompt_templates.prompt: Measure the mesh with the target process angle, then evaluate candidate orientations. Recommend the best option using support area and build height, with the tradeoff stated clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized redesign brief from the measured DfAM failures. Include the evidence field, target dimensions or angles, uncertainty, and the re-measurement step after CAD regeneration.

output_examples.input: Check this STL for FDM printing with a 45 degree self-supporting angle.
output: Watertightness: pass. The mesh is suitable for topology review.
Wall thickness: the sampled fifth percentile is below the FDM supported-wall limit. Thicken the affected region and re-measure.
Overhangs: report the measured down-facing area below 45 degrees and review orientation candidates.

output_examples.input: Which orientation should I use for this part?
output_examples.output: The recommended axis-aligned orientation is the candidate with the lowest support area, provided its build height remains acceptable. Treat the support estimate as a cost signal and verify the final choice in a slicer.

output_examples.input: Can this mesh be evaluated for SLS?
output_examples.output: Yes. Compare wall thickness and feature limits for SLS, but do not apply support-angle findings. Enclosed cavities still require a trapped-powder escape review because this tool does not measure it.

best_practices: Provide the target process, material, layer height, and machine datasheet when available.
Measure the exact uploaded mesh and cite both the measured field and the selected process limit.
Confirm units when the scale check reports a suspiciously small bounding-box diagonal.
anti_patterns: Do not infer printability from a render, generator script, or triangle count.
Do not silently rescale geometry or treat a sampled minimum as exhaustive proof.
Do not apply support-angle findings to powder processes or present support volume as slicer accuracy.

faq.question: Which mesh formats are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow supports STL, OBJ, PLY, and 3MF mesh files. STEP and STP files should be exported to an STL sidecar first.

faq.question: Does the skill run a slicer?
faq.answer: No. It measures geometry and reports comparisons. It does not slice, upload, start print jobs, or control a printer.

faq.question: Which printing processes are covered?
faq.answer: The reference includes FDM or FFF, SLS, SLA or DLP, metal PBF, and MJF.

faq.question: How reliable is wall thickness?
faq.answer: Wall thickness comes from ray-cast sampling. The sampled fifth percentile is a useful violation signal, but it is not an exhaustive inspection.

faq.question: Can it recommend an orientation?
faq.answer: It compares six axis-aligned orientations by support area and build height. It does not search arbitrary rotations or replace slicer verification.

faq.question: What does a need-more-information result mean?
faq.answer: It means the process context, geometry evidence, sampling quality, or a required measurement is missing. Provide more data before making a firm decision.
